messages.author: 36cda290860fb7b2
messages.subject: RE: paired analysis of two averages
parts:
Hi All,

I would like to compare the two reference sets both of which is a part
of a single data set using the CBS segmentation.
At the beginning I did a standard processsing of the whole data set
(normalization, summarization and FL correction) which results in
CnChipEffectSet "cesN".

Then I did:

ces1<-extract(cesN,arrays1)
ces2<-extract(cesN.arrays2)
cesRef1<-getAverageFile(ces1);
cesRef2<-getAverageFile(ces2);

then, naively, I tried

cbs<-CbsModel(cesRef1,cesRef2)

which did no work as the first argument should be CnChipEffectSet. and
cesRef1 is CnChipEffectFile

Is it possible and how can I convert CnChipEffectFile into
CnChipEffectSet (or may be the approach is plain wrong)?

I tried:
cr1 <- newInstance(ces1, cesRef1,
mergeStrands=ces$mergeStrands,combineAlleles=ces$combineAlleles)

but it does not work giving the exception:

[2008-08-04 16:13:20] Exception: Argument 'files' is of unknown type: logical

at newInstance(ces1, ceRef1, mergeStrands = ces$mergeStrands, combineAlleles =


Thank you,

Alex

See comments below.

On Mon, Aug 4, 2008 at 2:12 PM, Alex <alex.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Henrik,
>
> I 've install the 0.9.4 as you recommended. The problem is still
> exactly the same.

> Should I re-process the dataset again (I know it should be very fast
> 2nd time) ?

Yes, it is fast to rerun your script the 2nd time. It is always good
to start from a fresh R session when you have a problem so you can
rule out have old objects sitting around. The aroma.affymetrix
package is designed to detect and skip already processed steps, so the
overhead is quite small.

More comments below.

>> > I would like to compare the two reference sets both of which is a part
>> > of a single data set using the CBS segmentation.
Ok, comparing *two* references is a new use case.

>> > At the beginning I did a standard processsing of the whole data set
>> > (normalization, summarization and FL correction) which results in
>> > CnChipEffectSet "cesN".
>>
>> > Then I did:
>>
>> > ces1<-extract(cesN,arrays1)
>> > ces2<-extract(cesN.arrays2)
>> > cesRef1<-getAverageFile(ces1);
>> > cesRef2<-getAverageFile(ces2);
>>
>> > then, naively, I tried
>>
>> > cbs<-CbsModel(cesRef1,cesRef2)

So from this I conclude that you do not want to compare the set of
arrays in the two reference data sets, but rather the average of each
reference set. That is, cesRef1 and cesRef2 are as if they are two
hybridizations. Just to make this clear I would name the to object
like this instead (the 's' is for set):

cfRef1 <- getAverageFile(ces1);
cfRef2 <- getAverageFile(ces2);

>>
>> > which did no work as the first argument should be CnChipEffectSet. and
>> > cesRef1 is CnChipEffectFile
>>
>> > Is it possible and how can I convert CnChipEffectFile into
>> > CnChipEffectSet (or may be the approach is plain wrong)?
>>
>> > I tried:
>> > cr1 <- newInstance(ces1, cesRef1,
>> > mergeStrands=ces$mergeStrands,combineAlleles=ces$combineAlleles)

Almost. You have to pass a list of files, so instead do:

cesRef1 <- newInstance(ces1, list(cfRef1),
mergeStrands=ces1$mergeStrands,combineAlleles=ces1$combineAlleles);

This creates a *set* of the same class as 'ces1' containing one *file*.

Starting with aroma.affymetrix v0.9.4 you no longer have to do this
trick for the reference, so the following will work for you:

cbs <- CbsModel(cesRef1,cfRef2);

Hope this does what you want to do.

Cheers

Henrik
